public_sources: Godin & Thivierge 2026, PLOS Computational Biology, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719

actions: Retried read-only public recovery of S1 Code; file-level source remained unavailable in current transport.
Inspected the live paper's explicit acknowledgement that pseudoinverse/intrinsic-coordinate RLS could mitigate full-space conditioning and that SPLiT's novelty is online tracking.
Ran bounded source-derived paired controls using the same RLS solver class in tracked intrinsic versus full ambient coordinates.
Densified N=20..50 at T=3200, probed N down to 6, varied sample budget at N=20/50, isolated nuisance-noise dependence, and added algorithmic memory-state counts.
Persisted and read back role-local delta and LATEST pointer.

result_summary.main_result: After matching solver class, tracked intrinsic RLS beat full-space RLS across N=20..50 at T=3200 with all paired bootstrap CIs below zero; the prior N=20 reversal was largely a solver-class confound.
result_summary.negative_boundary: With zero synthetic nuisance noise, strong regularized full-space RLS and intrinsic RLS both reached essentially numerical-zero error, so low rank alone did not create a practical advantage in this bounded model.
result_summary.mechanism: The supported transferable mechanism is online subspace tracking plus denoised intrinsic-coordinate regression, with gains increasing under limited samples and higher ambient-to-intrinsic ratio; Oja-specific superiority remains unsupported.
result_summary.cost: Core persistent state changes from O(N^2) for full RLS to O(Nk) for tracking plus intrinsic RLS; at k=3 the core state-count reduction is 5.83x at N=20 and 15.74x at N=50.
